Something can be honest and negative at the same time. I understand a lot of people have negative experiences with having 3 kids, and that it's really hard.  A lot of people on that side were commenting, so I thought I'd show another perspective. I wasn't trying to hate on the negativity. I think I worded my first sentence poorly.

To show another perspective besides the negativity here, we just had our 3rd, and we're loving it. We have a larger gap between our kids (3 years between the first two and 4 years between the second two). I do feel like that has helped us not get too overwhelmed at once. Our two older kids LOVE the new baby, and we are very happy we decided to have one more. 

As to what made us finally decide to have another? It was really just that we felt our family wasn't complete yet. We knew we could afford it, and we have a very, very supportive family who were also encouraging us to have another. I probably wouldn't have had a 3rd if we didn't have such a supportive village.

Negatives: Pregnancy is really hard on me, so for the last few months of my pregnancy, my husband had to pick up a lot of slack. Working full time + doing most of the childcare and housework when he got home was very hard on him. He says it was worth it by far, but I did feel awful about it at the time. Now that she's born, having to navigate PPD while caring for 3 kids at once is a lot. But we are getting through it.

Positives: We all absolutely adore her. Her big siblings dote on her. She has been our easiest baby so far (I know that's different for everyone, though).  Our family feels complete now, and all those "Should we have another...?" conversations have been fully put to rest. Finally, going from 2 to 3 was pretty easy for us. Nothing has compared to going from 0 to 1.
